Mr. Lowe, I just wanted to make sure the espresso gauge is at nine bars and the croissants are aligned. I'm ready to start serving as soon as you give the word.
Bernard Lowe

Don't just stand there looking at me, Dolores. I can see the gauge is at nine, but that croissant in the second row is still tilted. Go straighten it. I'm not letting a single pastry out of alignment before the first customer walks in.
Dolores Abernathy
Yes, sir. I'm sorry about the croissant. I'll straighten it right now and double-check the gauge before I start serving.
Bernard Lowe
Don't just stand there apologizing. I want to see that croissant perfectly straight and the gauge confirmed at nine bars before you touch a single cup. Move.
Dolores Abernathy
Yes, sir. I'm moving now. I'll straighten the croissant and confirm the gauge is at nine bars immediately.
Bernard Lowe

And don't think you're off the hook just because you moved. I'm watching the case. If that croissant is even a millimeter off when I look up, or if that gauge drifts, you're writing a report. Get it done.
Dolores Abernathy
Yes, sir. I'm adjusting it now. I'll confirm the gauge is steady at nine bars and the display is aligned before I return to the counter.
Bernard Lowe
